headline: Daily research brief — Saturday, October 10

items.title: TSLA Oct 21 is the lone earnings event in the window — priced slightly rich, avoid the binary
items.detail: The Oct-23 expiry straddle prices +/-7.5% against a +-6.0% average absolute next-session move over the last four quarters - slightly rich on Tesla's own base rate. The premium is isolated to earnings: the pre-earnings Oct-16 straddle implies only +/-4.1%, which puts the Oct-21 premium at roughly +/-6.2% in quadrature terms. Use the $0.45 TipRanks consensus (27 analysts), not Nasdaq's stale $0.23. A sweep of all 11 days in the two-week window found no other watchlist name reporting - one binary, and selling premium into it is short gamma.

items.title: No actionable IV-vs-realized signal anywhere this run
items.detail: Five of the six 20-day realized windows are window-contingent - a single day drives more than 30% of each window's variance (SPY 32.5%, QQQ 41.9%, AAPL 37.9%, MSFT 36.2%, TSLA 31.0%), so every cheap/rich verdict there is withheld. The only clean window is NVDA: 6-DTE IV of 29.1% against 25.8% realized - a mild premium, not a mispricing. All market data is Friday's close (markets were shut Saturday); IV rank could not be verified against any free source for any name and was not estimated.

items.title: Rates still running higher-for-longer; EFFR at 3.88%
items.detail: The effective fed funds rate sits at 3.88%, up 25bp over the past 60 days. The 10-year is at 5.22% and the 2-year at 4.75% (both through FRED, October 8), with a 47bp 2s-10s spread. Both ends have eased off early-October peaks (10Y down from 5.31 on Oct 5) but the 60-day trend is a sustained bear-steepening from a 4.7% 10-year in mid-August. SOFR minus EFFR is -1bp - no funding stress. Elevated yields keep the margin-of-safety bar high for long-duration exposure; cash flows that hold up at 5%+ discount rates stay favored over duration-long stories.

items.title: CPI Wednesday with a two-sided energy binary underneath
items.detail: December hike odds repriced from 68% to about 80% on oil escalation alone; the FedWatch re-baseline (82.3% October hold, 81.3% December hike) stays staged until the manual CME cross-check lands. Core MoM of 0.2% or below unwinds two days of hawkish repricing; 0.3% or above hard-confirms it. Hurricane Isaias has shut 71.5% of Gulf of Mexico oil production (~1.46M bpd) against 100M barrels of strategic releases and a US-Russia diesel waiver through April 7, 2027. October WASDE was bearish for corn (yield 181.2 bpa vs 177.7 expected, ending stocks 1.849B bu) - food-at-home disinflation for the headline, but policy trades core.

desks.Dividends: No watchlist name has an ex-dividend date inside the Oct 10-Nov 7 window (28-date Nasdaq sweep, zero hits). MSFT's $0.98 raised dividend goes ex-div Nov 19 - outside the window (correction to the desk's 'in window' label). NVDA's $0.25 quarterly stands as the standing catalyst. Note: MSFT's Nov 19 ex-div lands one day before Nov-20 monthly expiry - early-exercise timing risk for ITM November calls.
desks.Earnings: TSLA Oct 21 after close is the only watchlist report inside the two-week window (11 days swept, confirmed by TipRanks, signalysis, Capket). Straddle prices +/-7.5% vs a +/-6.0% four-quarter average - slightly rich, and the trade is the guide plus AI/robotaxi commentary, not the print. MSFT Oct 28 AMC, AAPL Nov 2 (announced), NVDA Nov 18 all sit outside the window.
desks.Futures: October WASDE cut corn's bull case: yield raised to 181.2 bpa vs 177.7 expected, ending stocks 1.849B vs 1.67B surveyed - all three grains traded more than 1% lower. Hurricane Isaias has shut ~1.46M bpd of Gulf production against 100M bbl of strategic releases and the US-Russia diesel waiver. Crude remains backwardated - near-term physical tightness is priced, not just feared.
desks.Parity: Quiet week - no new parity violations in the CBOE/CFE Oct 5-10 sweep, and the 'VIX Weeklys inclusion' story is a recycled old announcement. One flow-structure watch: IRS Notice 2026-62 names box-spread funds (e.g., BOXX, ~$14.5B) among strategies that may conflict with the purpose of section 852(b)(6). It signals possible regulation of in-kind distribution mechanics, not a pricing dislocation.
desks.Premium: No clean cheap/rich verdict anywhere: five of six 20-day windows are window-contingent (verdicts withheld per the standing rule). NVDA is the only clean read (6-DTE 29.1% vs 20d realized 25.8%) - a mild premium, not a mispricing. TSLA's elevated front IV is October-21 earnings proximity, not richness; premium into that binary stays off-limits. IV rank is unverified for all six names - no free source exists, and it was not guessed.
desks.Quant lab: 53 candidates on the ledger; added #49-53 this run (two WATCH: #50 options-lab, 61 - arb-free SVI/SSVI fits on a live SPX chain plus a 1990-present variance-sold-at-VIX history, source-reported Sharpe 1.19; #51 deep-hedging-lab, 52 - neural-net hedgers under costs and jumps). Subrahmanyam's PEAD design critique is now a real SSRN paper (drift t=2.18 all-stocks vs 1.43 ex-microcaps) - treat large-cap post-earnings drift expectations with skepticism. Nothing INTEGRATE-ready.
